Hi everyone, I don't typically leave comments on videos.  But here goes.  I do agree with those that are unsatisfied with his advice.  Because its not for everyone.  I am currently working as a salaried motorcycle delivery boy.  I've been doing it for awhile now, it was never the job I envisioned myself doing 7 years before 27.  But I work with the opportunities I am given.  When your bank account grows, so do your opportunities to live the life you want to live.  I am a huge fan of the work-cation idea.  For example, if you've been working your 38 hr / week job and feel like you just cannot go on.  Book yourself an airbnb or coworking coliving space.  Spend a bit of money on your experience.  You keep working as to not get let go of, but you change your routine.  You know, get out of your house or head.  I'd prefer to do something else but I cannot deny that working has given me many blessings in forms of opportunities.  And now I get to take care of myself on my own, and at this point it is empowering me.  I watched this video because I am looking for a career switch and move myself to a bigger city with more exciting opportunities.  But it is important to know your local cities well, and to know which opportunities are within your grasp and make the most sense.

One of the massive areas for profitable employment in the future is in  dramatically simplifying access and use of business and reactional software. At present, computer companies expect the consumer to do most of the heavy lifting in the new age . There is very little personal memory so we have to tediously fill in information over and over, the security systems are ludicrous with multiple checks even after password entries. We are expected to download files and print paper costing us money, rather than companies. Much of what is claimed to be making life easier for consumers is just shifting the burden from companies to consumers. Those people who design integrated and intuitive systems that can be used automatically  by the non tech savvy as well as nerds will make a fortune, as well as positively transforming our society. Computer developers are currently the victims of their own delusions!

I’m 28, working in CISF as a Head Constable/Ministerial, earning around ₹46K in hand. Alongside my job, I’m constantly learning—AI tools and their practical applications, communication, macroeconomics, geopolitics, pattern recognition, and how all of these things ultimately affect our everyday lives and finances.
I live alone in a government quarter, cook my own food, manage the household, handle my daily office responsibilities, and work in a force where holidays are practically nonexistent—Sunday second half is usually the only real break.
And honestly, I feel more alive than ever.
I quit Instagram a few months ago, and I’ve realized that my happiness doesn’t come from endless scrolling or comparing my life with others. It comes from learning, building, becoming more capable, and understanding the world around me.
And Ishan, thank you. I’m genuinely learning so much from you every day. Your content has helped me look at my career, money, skills, and the world from a much broader perspective.
Still learning. Still building. Still figuring things out.

I consume a lot of content on YouTube, and sometimes X, and I love to pour my thoughts out on the content I consume — mostly in English. Earlier, I would myself edit the comment, then by ChatGPT, and only thereafter I would make it live on the comment box. But now I have made a change: I now mostly check for grammatical correctness only after droping the comment. It is because now I feel that I make mistakes but not so much that I need to edit it before commenting on such platforms where our identity is almost completely obscure.
